title: Bridgeboard: OKR-aligned dependency register & cutover playbook
creator: Nora Patel
description: Create a lightweight, persistent dependency register (the 'Bridgeboard') that maps initiative-level OKRs and milestones to concrete cross-team handoffs (Engineering, Design, Security, Infra). The Bridgeboard will power early-warning signals, automated notifications before cutovers, and a standardized cutover playbook with owner assignments and rollback criteria. Objective: reduce missed handoffs and last-minute escalations across roadmap cutovers by 50% for Q2 initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Bridgeboard UI + API accessible in Console with searchable entries for every active initiative
Automated weekly readiness snapshot emailed to owners and slotted into cycle rituals
Cutover playbook template available with explicit pre-cutover checks, security gating steps, and rollback paths
Two pilot initiatives complete full Bridgeboard lifecycle with documented lessons and zero customer-impact incidents
OKR linkage: each dependency is tagged to an initiative OKR and rollup metric
milestones: M1: Schema and minimum viable fields defined (2026-03-10)
M2: API + console listing + PRD published (2026-03-24)
M3: Pilot integrations with Eng/Design/Security/Infra + first readiness snapshot (2026-04-08)
M4: Cutover playbook finalized and runbook published (2026-04-15)
deliverables: Console listing with filter by OKR/initiative/owner/status
Weekly readiness snapshot generator (email + Slack digest)
Cutover playbook template and postmortem checklist
risks: Teams do not reliably update dependency status -> stale register
Security gating adds friction to cutovers if review turnaround is long
Integration work for legacy infra services takes longer than estimated

notes: This work focuses on reducing cross-team friction during roadmap cutovers by tying dependencies explicitly to OKRs and providing a lightweight operational workflow. The Bridgeboard intentionally limits scope to active initiatives and adds an opt-in pilot flag for teams to avoid adding noise to day-to-day tickets. Expect follow-up PM tickets for scaling and automation after pilot lessons.
implementation_strategy: Phase 1: schema + minimal console listing + API for manual entry. Phase 2: readiness snapshots and Slack/email integrations. Phase 3: enrich with automated probes and runtime signals (latency/cost regressions) and integrate into release gating.
